subject: Show position of individual response on histogram

messages.author: bb70ad83fe774fb1
messages.subject: Show position of individual response on histogram
parts:
Hi,

Please excuse my naivety as I am very new to r and ggplot2.

I have managed to create histograms using ggplot for a set of blood glucose results and showed different methods used for testing in the graph. However I would like to share these with all people who submitted a glucose result.

Is it possible to create individual-specific histograms i.e. a histogram showing/flagging position of an individual's response?

Thanks,
MavF

parts: My first reaction would to be to loop over each person and then create a column that is called `Is.your.result` that is TRUE for that person’s results (FALSE otherwise) and then in your `geom_historgram` call use `aes([your other code], fill = Is.your.result)`

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Show position of individual response on histogram
parts:
Hi:

To expand on Doug's suggestion, here's a very simple outline of how
you might apply a function to generate a plot for each patient.

DF <- data.frame(id = seq_len(100),
x = rnorm(100))

library(ggplot2)

myplot <- function(dat, i, ...)
{
d <- dat[i, ] # Sub-data frame for patient i

library(ggplot2)
p <- ggplot(dat, aes(x = x)) +
geom_histogram(fill = "darkorange", ...) +
geom_vline(data = d, aes(xintercept = x), size = 1)
ggsave(paste0("patient", i, ".pdf"), plot = p)
}

for(i in 1:3) myplot(DF, i)


In the function, you might want to create a patient-specific title and
it might be useful to make an annotation of the observed glucose level
of each patient. These can be added by modifying the myplot() function
appropriately. The purpose of the ... argument as a formal of myplot
is so that you can pass arguments to geom_histogram() in the call,
e.g., binwidth. You could also do the same with geom_vline() if you
like. You might also want to substitute a point in place of a line; if
so, change geom_vline() to geom_point(). The point is that the
function should be edited to suit your needs.

I just plotted the first three to show proof of concept.

For reporting purposes, I'd suggest looking into something like the
brew package to create individualized reports for each case in an
automated way, if this is not already familiar to you. For that
purpose, it might be useful to save the plots to a list instead (thus
removing the ggsave() line) and then write a template report function
that grabs personal information from a patient's row in the data frame
and the plots from the list, in sequence. Several people have blogged
about this, so look on-line for details - IIRC, there's a way to do
this straightforwardly with knitr and RStudio.

Dennis
